title: U.S. House · Ohio's 7th District
area: Northeast Ohio, including parts of Cuyahoga, Lorain, and Medina counties

context.text: The Cook Political Report rates the 7th District R+5. Eight Democrats ran in the primary, the most candidates for any Ohio U.S. House district in 2026; Brian Poindexter won with 37.0% of the vote.

Two independent write-in candidates, Thahbia Asad and Andrey Martinichin, are also seeking write-in votes in the general election; they do not appear as printed ballot lines and are not profiled here.

candidates.name: Max Miller
candidates.ballotNote: Incumbent, unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Miller is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Ohio's 7th District, first elected in 2022. He previously served as director of presidential advance and a senior advisor in the first Trump administration.

background.text: Born in Ohio in 1988; earned a bachelor's degree in history from Cleveland State University (2013).
Served in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserves and worked as director of presidential advance and a senior advisor in the first Trump administration before being elected to Congress.

positions.summary: In a September 2026 Akron Beacon Journal candidate Q&A he said he does not support tariffs, but that he did not go against his party's president after the Supreme Court declared them legal.
positions.quote: I don't support tariffs, however, once the Supreme Court declared they were legal, I wasn't going to go against my party's president just as any Democrat wouldn't.

positions.summary: In the same Q&A he said he supports Ohio's proposed proof-of-citizenship voting requirement and has supported the federal SAVE America Act.
positions.quote: I support the law Ohio is putting on the ballot this year, requiring proof of citizenship prior to voting. I have also supported the SAVE America Act on the federal level.

record.text: Served on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology and the Committee on Agriculture during the 118th Congress (2023-2024).

candidates.name: Brian Poindexter
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 37.0% in an eight-candidate field

summary.text: Poindexter is a union ironworker and apprenticeship instructor running as the Democratic nominee, with an at-large seat on the Brook Park City Council. His platform centers on workers' rights, wages, and healthcare.

background.text: Earned an associate degree from Cuyahoga Community College; has worked as a union ironworker and, as of 2026, as an apprenticeship instructor for Ironworkers Local 17.
Served as an at-large member of the Brook Park City Council.

priorities.text: Campaign website says the economy should be 'built from the foundation up' by workers, criticizing policies he says protect corporate profits over wages.
priorities.quote: An economy that works can't be built from the penthouse down. It has to be built from the foundation up, and workers are that foundation.

priorities.text: Campaign website supports the right to organize and says unions 'raise standards not just for their members, but for entire industries.'
Campaign website says healthcare 'shouldn't disappear when a job does' and calls for healthcare that is portable and not tied to employment.

positions.summary: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (2026) he says he supports expanding access to unions and raising the minimum wage.
positions.quote: I support expanding access to unions and raising the minimum wage.

positions.summary: In a September 2026 Akron Beacon Journal Q&A he said he supports undoing the health care cuts in the 2025 budget law and working toward universal health care over time.
positions.quote: I support working towards universal health care over time.

positions.summary: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (2026) he says he opposes blanket tariffs while saying targeted tariffs can be a tool.
positions.quote: I oppose the blanket tariffs that are making everything more expensive.

positions.summary: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (2026) he says he wants to end the tax cuts for the wealthy.
positions.quote: end the tax cuts for the wealthy

positions.summary: In a September 2026 Akron Beacon Journal Q&A he said he supports Ohio's 2024 reproductive-rights amendment and would oppose bills that threaten women or doctors with jail time.
positions.quote: In 2024, Ohio voted to protect a woman's right to make her own decisions about reproductive health care. I support that law, and I will oppose any bills that would threaten women or doctors with jail time.
